content.title: About
content.content: Stewed chitterlings are a traditional Puerto Rican dish consisting of slowly simmered pork intestines flavored with garlic, oregano, vinegar, olive oil, and aromatic spices such as adobo and cumin. The dish is often served with rice, beans, and plantains, and appears as a festive appetizer at family gatherings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chitterlings have been prepared in Puerto Rico for over 300 years.
Traditional preparation includes a pre‑soak in vinegar to remove odor.
The dish is commonly cooked in a "parrilló," a clay pot that retains moisture and flavor.
In Puerto Rican culture, chitterlings symbolize frugality and nose‑to‑tail cooking.
A sweet‑potato version exists, adding a subtle sweetness to the stew.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork intestines provide a rich source of complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Good source of iron
items.content: Iron in chitterlings helps maintain hemoglobin levels and prevents anemia.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system health and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish fits well into low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugar.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Pork intestines can harbor harmful bacteria; thorough cooking to safe internal temperature is essential.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: Chitterlings are cholesterol‑rich, so people with heart disease should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to pork proteins.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Elevated purines can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve stewed chitterlings hot, typically alongside rice, beans, fried plantains, or mashed potatoes. They can be sliced and added to stews, tacos, or used as a sandwich filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked chitterlings in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
